title: BI creation: choose a mode, then verify readiness
summary: Choose native OneLake, empty, generated, or authored semantic-model creation; distinguish an empty bound report from PBIR visual authoring. Covers source compatibility, cross-workspace access, framing, bounded verification, and safe recovery without silent binding changes.

semantic_model_decisions.intent: Use known compatible Delta tables without local definition files
semantic_model_decisions.notes: Repeat the flag up to 100 times with canonical HTTPS OneLake DFS table URLs. The service infers tables/columns. Do not add --connection, --file, or --definition. Cross-workspace sources require access to every source data item. Native creation does not perform Fabio's SQL/TDS schema discovery.

semantic_model_decisions.intent: Create a deliberately empty starting point
semantic_model_decisions.path: semantic-model create without definition or OneLake-table inputs
semantic_model_decisions.notes: An empty model is a shell, not a model over existing tables. Do not add --connection. Inspect and author it before expecting data queries or a useful report.

semantic_model_decisions.intent: Generate a definition from lakehouse/warehouse metadata
semantic_model_decisions.notes: This remains a separate, useful definition-backed path. Both storage modes read the SQL endpoint over TDS and need SQL-audience credentials. Choose --storage-mode onelake for direct OneLake binding or sql for SQL-endpoint binding; do not silently change the chosen security/fallback behavior. The generator handles schema-less lakehouses and requests framing unless --no-refresh is supplied; submission is not completion.

--definition takes a complete model folder with definition.pbism and its model body. --file takes one model file; multiple --file flags are invalid. Preserve an authored folder's source expressions. --connection is a definition-backed option, not a universal prerequisite and not a substitute for checking the actual expressions/partitions.

report_decisions.intent: Create an empty report already bound to a model
report_decisions.notes: Native creationPayload mode supplies no definition. --semantic-model-workspace defaults to the report workspace; provide it for cross-workspace references and check source-model access. This does not author a dashboard or guarantee an enhanced PBIR format.

report_decisions.path: report scaffold then report validate and report create --definition
report_decisions.notes: Use real model fields, scaffold a PBIR folder, validate offline, then publish. --dataset rebinds an authored folder's model reference. Native --semantic-model is mutually exclusive with --dataset/--definition/--file; it is not an alias for --dataset in other commands.

report_decisions.intent: Use the existing generated blank-report definition
report_decisions.notes: This compatibility path synthesizes definition.pbir plus a PBIR-Legacy report.json. It remains supported but is not the preferred starting point for enhanced-PBIR-only editing. Inspect the stored format before editing an existing report.

source_checks: Source checking is integrated as an explicit opt-in gate: native create --one-lake-table ... --check-source and both generator storage modes share the standalone semantic-model check-source engine. Every requested finding must be ready before creation POST; unknown/partial evidence stops with sourceCheck and no mode switch. Existing calls do not gain extra source reads/permissions. Authored/empty create sources are not guessed. See bi-source-preflight for bounds, supported evidence and limitations.

Inspect the actual Delta source and source schema. SQL views are not Delta-table fixtures. A syntactically valid URL does not prove source existence, permissions, compatible table schema, or loaded data.

Schema-qualified URLs on a schema-enabled lakehouse are live-validated. A schema-less native source returned DirectLakeSchemaError because the service assumed dbo. Explain this compatibility issue and offer an explicit generator/authored alternative; do not silently retry with different binding semantics.

Watch for inferred table-name collisions when selecting tables from multiple sources. Having permission to create in the target workspace does not prove read permission on a different source workspace.
readiness: semantic-model refresh returns an additive submission receipt and top-level refreshId. generate returns the same receipt under framing plus refreshId; legacy framed means acknowledgement only, not completion, and false does not prove rejection when framing.state is unknown. no-refresh is explicitly skipped. Inspect state, correlationStatus and completionStatus separately.

Only a canonical Location for the EXACT workspace/model/refresh route establishes refreshId; it is parsed, never followed. Origins must match the configured endpoint, except the public Power BI API's live-verified HTTPS regional *.analysis.windows.net alias (port 443). Arbitrary origins remain invalid. x-ms-request-id is retained as a transport trace and, if present, must agree with the Location UUID; a trace alone never becomes a refresh ID. Missing, malformed, duplicate, wrong-scope/origin or conflicting metadata leaves refreshId null without discarding acknowledgement. No latest-history fallback or alternate submission is attempted.

A successful HTTP acknowledgement with an unreadable body retains the receipt and verified header identity instead of becoming a retryable submission failure. Error-bearing success bodies remain unknown. Unknown network/server outcomes are non-retriable because work may already be running. The generator keeps the created model and a sanitized unknown/rejected framing receipt rather than telling callers to blindly submit again.

Use semantic-model readiness --workspace <WS> --id <MODEL> for bounded metadata/schema observations across native/generated/authored modes. Add repeatable --expected-table names (maximum 20) to assert the intended model tables. INFO.VIEW schema visibility is NOT source Delta/protocol validation; schema is capped at 200 tables and truncation/malformed/conflicting evidence stays unknown.

Data reads are opt-in: --probe-data with --expected-table executes one COUNTROWS result query over those tables. --min-rows 1 requires each to be nonempty; the default minimum 0 permits empty but queryable tables. This may scan data/consume capacity. Success establishes only those counts under this caller, not freshness, effective access for others, or Direct Lake instead of DirectQuery fallback.

Select --refresh-id using the receipt's refreshId only when correlationStatus is verified; inspect one EXACT request endpoint, never latest/older history. Missing, unknown or conflicting completion evidence stays unknown. Explicit terminal refresh failure is checked before schema/data queries, avoiding an unnecessary scan. If no verified identity is exposed, correlate new IDs against a pre-submission refresh-status baseline where available; ambiguous correlation needs review, not another submission. No refresh is submitted by readiness.

Select --report-id and optional --report-workspace (default model workspace) to compare the Power BI datasetId binding with the selected model. A matching UUID is binding evidence even when datasetWorkspaceId is not reported; the report records that omission. Binding does not prove pages/visuals exist/render or viewer access. No rebind or definition read/write is performed.

Readiness is one snapshot unless --wait is given. Waiting repeats only reads, with --max-attempts (default 6, maximum 20), --interval (default 5), and a TOTAL --timeout (default 30, maximum 300 seconds) including in-flight queries, retries and sleeps. It stops on ready or an explicitly failed/cancelled/disabled selected refresh. --strict prints the report then exits non-zero unless all requested checks are ready. Review notChecked: omitted data/refresh/report checks are never inferred from successful schema reads.

DAX executeQueries now works under --readonly through a narrowly constrained query transport. Refresh/create/takeover/definition changes still use mutation guards. Malformed, error-bearing or multi-result HTTP-200 DAX envelopes fail instead of appearing as an empty successful result. No arbitrary endpoint is accepted by the read-only POST path.
Successful creation means the artifact exists, not that it is query-ready or complete as a business model.

semantic-model refresh returns refresh_triggered after submitting work. Poll refresh-status for the new request with a bounded deadline and interval; stop on failure. Do not repeatedly submit refresh while waiting or treat an earlier completed refresh as proof of the new one.

After framing, inspect model tables/columns/measures/relationships and verify a bounded DAX read before binding visuals. Direct Lake avoids importing source data; it does not eliminate framing or readiness checks. The generator's legacy framed:true flag means refresh SUBMITTED, not completed; its note directs bounded verification rather than a fixed sleep.
Inspect report definition.pbir to verify the intended model binding, and inspect pages/visuals for authored reports. An empty bound report is not a finished report.
safety: Preview mutations with --dry-run. Readiness checks must not silently create credentials/connections, grant access, take ownership, change runtime/capacity policy, or purge data.
Changing native/generator/storage modes can change binding and security semantics. Explain the alternative and preserve the user's choice.
Model/report edits overwrite definitions. Review the intended change; --allow-purge-data and takeover are never automatic error-recovery steps.
